What it represents: Transaction-level sales fact table. Each row represents one completed sales transaction for one product, customer, store and date.
Calendar dimension used for date slicing and time-intelligence calculations.
Product master dimension containing product attributes such as category, subcategory and brand.
Customer master dimension containing demographic, geography and customer-segment attributes.
Store master dimension containing store, city, state and region attributes.
FactSales: SaleID; DimDate: DateKey; DimProduct: ProductKey; DimCustomer: CustomerKey; DimStore: StoreKey.
FactSales.DateKey, FactSales.ProductKey, FactSales.CustomerKey and FactSales.StoreKey reference the corresponding dimension keys.
Create four 1:* relationships from each dimension key to the matching FactSales foreign key.
Use Single cross-filter direction from each dimension (1 side) to FactSales (many side).
In Power BI, select DimDate and choose Table tools → Mark as date table, using DimDate[Date].
DateKey is an integer YYYYMMDD key and should be related to FactSales[DateKey]. The actual DimDate[Date] column should be used for time-intelligence functions.
Use a star schema: dimensions around FactSales; avoid bidirectional relationships unless a specific modeling requirement justifies them.
Create measures rather than calculated columns for most DAX practice questions so you can observe filter context changes in visuals.
